title: Learning string bass and other string instruments by ear
summary: He learned the tuba first, then picked up string bass from his violin, guitar and mandolin background, not by reading music.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: One more short question about your string bass. Did you have any lessons on that? Where did you learn to play it as well as you do? You play it so fine and that wonderful tone and the good rhythm style.
Well, that's the only, that's the one I learned my music up there.
On the tuba? Yeah. But then you picked up the string bass yourself?
Yeah, I picked up the string bass, so when I was a little bit of boy. Just from knowing the violin?

I used to play the ghetto. Jim had a ghetto and I'd learn on that. And the mandolin, I'd learn on that, you see. Well, that made me play the little fiddle by head, the drum, no I mean the ghetto by head, and the mandolin.
Well, you played that all the string.

I just learned that, just as a sideline, you know. I wasn't doing nothing. I'd pick up, I'd learn how to play the mandolin so good, but my mother, I was a small fellow, you know, and she said, well, I'm going to get you a fiddle, let you learn how to play a violin. I'd learn everything they'd get. I'm sorry, I didn't learn the violin with music, you know. But, it was alright.
